hidden_dual_route_1.name: {name}
hidden_dual_route_1.text: *As I finish cleaning up after the event, I put the literature club critique copy and first-aid card in my bag.*

hidden_dual_route_choice.name: {name}
hidden_dual_route_choice.text: *I take out one of the two records first. None of these relationships need to be decided today.*
choices: Open the literature club critique copy

hidden_perfect_homeroom_1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_1.text: *On graduation day, my homeroom teacher hands me a copy of my recommendation and my reading record.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_1b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_1b.text: *At the door of the empty classroom, she sorts the literature club critique copies. Each manuscript is marked only with a student number.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_2.text: Congratulations on graduating. Your recommendation and reading record are in the envelope. Check at home that nothing is missing.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_2c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_2c.text: The critique helped me finish it. I sent it to a publisher too. Whatever happens is mine to handle. You take care of yourself.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3.text: *After the classroom door closed that day, we had no private contact. Four years later, {name} had graduated from college and was living alone near their first job.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3b.text: *At a bookstore café on my way home from work, I spot a familiar name on a poster for a new-book talk. When I look up, she sees me too.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3c.text: What a coincidence. *She sets down the event materials.* If you have time, would you like to sit?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3e.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3e.text: I'm still teaching at the same school. And I published a book. — What kind of work are you doing these days?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3f.text: Would you like to meet here again? There's a lot we didn't get to talk about today.

hidden_perfect_homeroom_3g.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_3g.text: *We save our names and numbers in each other's phones—information that was never part of the old school contact list.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4b.text: *At our second meeting, she takes a copy of her book from the shelf.* This time it's the published edition. Will you read it and tell me what you think?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4c.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4c.text: *I return to the home I live in alone and read the book until dawn—this time, at a reader's pace.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4d.text: *At our next meeting in the café, she stirs her coffee once and lets go of the spoon.* What did you think?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4e.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4e.text: *At our third meeting, after work, my former homeroom teacher is already waiting on a café terrace overlooking the cherry blossoms with a small bouquet.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4f.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4f.text: *She places the bouquet in the middle of the table and straightens its ribbon.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_4g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_perfect_homeroom_4g.text: It's a gift to celebrate the publication. And may I take it to mean you'd like to see me again?

hidden_perfect_homeroom_5.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_5.text: *We stand side by side outside the café door. Holding the bouquet, she waits for my answer instead of walking ahead.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep1.text: *We spend longer talking about the past four years than about school.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep2.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep2.text: *We take turns choosing our next plans: Thursdays are hers, Saturdays are {name}'s.*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep3.text: *Her second book is published. Instead of a specific name, the dedication reads, 'To the readers who stayed to the end and answered in their own words.'*

hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep4.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_homeroom_ep4.text: *Our shared calendar contains only each other's workdays and plans for the next weekend. The titles we used at school remain only in the caption on a graduation photo from four years ago.*

hidden_true_homeroom_1.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_1.text: *Four years after graduation. The two have had no private contact in all that time. After leaving school, graduating from college, and learning to support themself, {name} spots a book-talk poster bearing a familiar name at an independent bookstore on the way home from work.*

hidden_true_homeroom_2.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_2.text: *After the event, the signing table finally clears. The author, dressed in a beige cardigan, looks up from arranging her books.*

hidden_true_homeroom_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_2_b.text: *A company ID hangs from {name}'s neck. In her hands is a book printed with her own name instead of an attendance register.*

hidden_true_homeroom_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_3.text: It's been a long time. What should I call you now?

hidden_true_homeroom_3_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_3_b.text: Call me by my name. I'm not a student anymore.

hidden_true_homeroom_3_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_3_c.text: Let's take that slowly. You came as a reader today, right?

hidden_true_homeroom_4.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4.text: *She checks the name and photo on my company ID in turn.* You've really built a life of your own.

hidden_true_homeroom_4_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_4_b.text: *Before school comes up, we talk about our jobs and the books we've been reading lately.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_c.text: *She takes a book from the display. It has the same title as the manuscript once kept in her desk.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4_d.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_d.text: I finished it in the end. I spent a long time with the critique the literature club gave me back then.

hidden_true_homeroom_4_e.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_4_e.text: Do you remember the marks I left?

hidden_true_homeroom_4_f.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_f.text: We agreed I wouldn't try to identify anyone's comments. I do remember that someone left an unusual number of questions on the final page.

hidden_true_homeroom_4_g.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_g.text: *She squares the corner of the book once. She doesn't fold the cup sleeve the way she used to.*

hidden_true_homeroom_4_h.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_4_h.text: The event's over—do you have time? I'd like to get coffee. If that would make you uncomfortable, we can just say goodbye here.

hidden_true_homeroom_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_5.text: I'd like to get to know who you are now, not the student you used to be.

hidden_true_homeroom_5_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_5_b.text: *She waits for {name}'s answer instead of walking toward the register.*

hidden_true_homeroom_5_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_5_c.text: I'd like to get to know who you are now too. We can take our time deciding what to call each other.

hidden_true_homeroom_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_6.text: Good. Then coffee first. We can talk about the rest over a cup.

hidden_true_homeroom_6_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_6_b.text: *On the walk to the café, we ask about each other's commutes and current work.*

hidden_true_homeroom_7.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_7.text: I'd like that. And I'd like to make another plan too.

hidden_true_homeroom_7_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_7_b.text: *Smiling, she takes out her phone and shows her contact screen first, then waits.*

hidden_true_homeroom_7_c.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_7_c.text: Starting today, let's not force ourselves to erase the old title. But let's learn each other's names again first.

hidden_true_homeroom_7_d.name: {name}
hidden_true_homeroom_7_d.text: *I say her name once. She slowly says {name}'s in return.*

hidden_true_homeroom_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_true_homeroom_8.text: *Beyond the cake plate, she opens her palm and stops before making contact, waiting for {name}'s answer.* Would you like to meet again next week?

hidden_good_homeroom_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_good_homeroom_1.text: *After the graduation ceremony, she calls {name} over while sorting copies of recommendation letters and the literature club's critique packet in the empty classroom.* These are your records. Check that nothing's missing.

hidden_good_homeroom_2.name: {name}
hidden_good_homeroom_2.text: *I take the envelope, and we walk out into the hall together. The last students head down the stairs while my homeroom teacher gathers the remaining manuscripts and papers in her arms.*

hidden_good_homeroom_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_good_homeroom_3.text: Keep writing. I'll finish my manuscript. Let's each focus on our own work first.

hidden_good_homeroom_4.name: {name}
hidden_good_homeroom_4.text: *After saying goodbye, {name} walks to the end of the hall and looks back. The homeroom teacher stands by the window, seeing the graduates off. They give her a small bow, then leave the school.*

hidden_bitter_homeroom_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_bitter_homeroom_1.text: *After the graduation ceremony, she reads the letter {name} handed her in the empty classroom, then carefully sets it on the desk.* I can't keep this.

hidden_bitter_homeroom_2.name: {name}
hidden_bitter_homeroom_2.text: *The letter comes back with its corners smoothed flat.*

hidden_bitter_homeroom_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_bitter_homeroom_3.text: I believed in your writing, and I did care about you as my student. But I can't answer you in the way you want.

hidden_bitter_homeroom_4.name: {name}
hidden_bitter_homeroom_4.text: *She places the letter on top of the recommendation envelope and returns both. The classroom door stands open to the hall.*

hidden_bitter_homeroom_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_bitter_homeroom_5.text: Congratulations on graduating. I do wonder what you'll write next, but I can't promise to be there beside you.

hidden_bitter_homeroom_6.name: {name}
hidden_bitter_homeroom_6.text: *I gather the letter and recommendation and leave the classroom. I don't look back, and no one calls my name from behind.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_1.text: *Five years after graduation. I've worked away from home and lived alone for two years. At a local weekend health event, I spot a familiar name on the first-aid instructor's badge: Lee Juwon.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_2.text: *After the event, she removes the badge from her coat.* {name}? I never expected to see you here.

hidden_perfect_nurse_3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_3.text: *We sit across from each other at a café opposite the venue. The practice bandages remain packed in their box.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_3b.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_3b.text: I used to be responsible for your counseling. Are you sure you're comfortable sitting down with me like this now?

hidden_perfect_nurse_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_4.text: If you're uncomfortable, we can stop at hello. I was only curious how you've been.

hidden_perfect_nurse_4b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_4b.text: I'm comfortable. And today, I'd rather hear about you than about school.

hidden_perfect_nurse_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_perfect_nurse_5.text: Then shall we make our next meeting neither treatment nor counseling?

hidden_perfect_nurse_5b.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_5b.text: *We compare calendars until we find a Saturday when we're both free.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep1.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep1.text: *Several months later. After spending a number of weekends together, we wake to the same morning for the first time. Juwon reaches out beneath the covers and waits with her fingers loosely open.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep2.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep2.text: *After that morning at Juwon's home, the weekends in our shared calendar filled one by one. In the meantime, Juwon transferred to the education team at a university hospital, where the new nurses began calling her Instructor Lee as well. Instructor Lee Juwon.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep3.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep3.text: *The rosemary plant sits on the windowsill of the home we chose together. We take turns watering it.*

hidden_perfect_nurse_ep4.name: {name}
hidden_perfect_nurse_ep4.text: *One line remains on the final page of the pale green notebook: 'It took a long time, but now I'll begin again by my own choice.'*

hidden_true_nurse_1.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_1.text: *Four years after graduation. One spring evening, a year after moving out on my own, I hear a familiar voice at a local health campaign booth on my way home from work.*

hidden_true_nurse_2.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_2.text: *After the event, we sit across from each other again at a nearby café. The bandages and leaflets from the booth are packed away in her bag.*

hidden_true_nurse_2_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_2_b.text: *Two company IDs from different workplaces rest on the table. One phone shows an overtime-approval notice; the other, a report that the health event has ended.*

hidden_true_nurse_2_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_2_c.text: It's been a long time. Have you been well?

hidden_true_nurse_2_d.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_2_d.text: Yes. I have a job now too, and I live on my own.

hidden_true_nurse_3.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_3.text: Even what we call each other is complicated. Would it feel strange if you still called me 'teacher'?

hidden_true_nurse_3_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_3_b.text: We can change that slowly. There's no rush.

hidden_true_nurse_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_4.text: I remember you walking in dizzy on your first day after transferring.

hidden_true_nurse_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5.text: Back then, we were teacher and student, so that was where it ended.

hidden_true_nurse_5_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_5_b.text: *Juwon lets go of her coffee cup and waits for {name}'s answer.*

hidden_true_nurse_5_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5_c.text: Now we've met again by chance.

hidden_true_nurse_5_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5_d.text: So I'll ask: would you like to meet again?

hidden_true_nurse_5_f.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_5_f.text: *She taps the coffee-cup handle twice with one finger.* Right. A bandage should take under three minutes.

hidden_true_nurse_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_6.text: If this makes you uncomfortable, we can end it here. If not, I'd like to see you again next week.

hidden_true_nurse_7.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_7.text: *We leave the café and walk side by side to the subway station. Neither of us changes direction to follow the other.*

hidden_true_nurse_7_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_7_b.text: You can answer about next week after you get home.

hidden_true_nurse_7_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_7_c.text: It isn't a no. I'd like to see you again too.

hidden_true_nurse_7_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_7_d.text: *She takes out her phone and opens her calendar.* Then next weekend. We'll find a day that works for both of us.

hidden_true_nurse_8.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8.text: Next time, let's meet without needing a health event as an excuse.

hidden_true_nurse_8_b.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_b.text: *For three months, we meet at a different café every weekend. That day, Juwon invites me to her home for the first time.*

hidden_true_nurse_8_c.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_c.text: *We choose a movie and sit side by side on the sofa. It is dark outside, and the two cups of coffee on the table slowly go cold.*

hidden_true_nurse_8_d.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_d.text: *We don't spend long talking about school. There is more to say about work now and next weekend.*

hidden_true_nurse_8_e.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8_e.text: Back then, I did think about leaving the school.

hidden_true_nurse_8_f.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_f.text: But staying was your choice, wasn't it?

hidden_true_nurse_8_g.name: School Nurse
hidden_true_nurse_8_g.text: Right. I chose it—not because anyone held me there. Coming here today was my choice too.

hidden_true_nurse_8_h.name: {name}
hidden_true_nurse_8_h.text: Then I'll come by next week, too. That's my choice. *Before the movie ends, Juwon falls asleep against {name}'s shoulder.*

hidden_good_nurse_1.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_1.text: *After the graduation ceremony, the nurse's office door opens one last time. Juwon is drinking coffee by the window. When she sees {name}, she sets down her cup.* What brings you here? You shouldn't have anything wrong with you today.

hidden_good_nurse_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_2.text: If you came to say goodbye before you leave, sit down. As of today, your treatment here is over.

hidden_good_nurse_2_c.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_2_c.text: *After a moment's thought, she nods.* Okay. If you get hurt, don't tough it out—go to a hospital first. I won't be able to check on you anymore.

hidden_good_nurse_2_d.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_2_d.text: *She takes the pale green notebook from her desk drawer and opens it to the last page.*

hidden_good_nurse_3.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_3.text: *Juwon writes the date and 'Graduated, no issues' before closing the notebook. This time, she gives me neither a bandage nor her contact information.*

hidden_good_nurse_3_b.name: School Nurse
hidden_good_nurse_3_b.text: Take care. Next time we run into each other, say hello as a graduate, not a patient.

hidden_good_nurse_4.name: {name}
hidden_good_nurse_4.text: *Before leaving the nurse's office, I look back. Juwon sits by the window with her coffee cup in hand. We exchange a small bow.*

hidden_bitter_nurse_1.name: {name}
hidden_bitter_nurse_1.text: *After the graduation ceremony, I stop by the nurse's office one last time and hand over the pale green record card with a note bearing my contact information tucked underneath.*

hidden_bitter_nurse_2.name: School Nurse
hidden_bitter_nurse_2.text: *Juwon reads the note in silence. Then she folds it neatly along the crease and slides it back.* I shouldn't accept this.

hidden_bitter_nurse_3.name: {name}
hidden_bitter_nurse_3.text: Was I a nuisance, coming here so often?

hidden_bitter_nurse_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_bitter_nurse_4.text: You were never a nuisance. That's why I can't leave you confused. I looked after you because you were a student and you were hurt.

hidden_bitter_nurse_5.name: {name}
hidden_bitter_nurse_5.text: *Juwon writes ‘Graduation, counseling concluded’ on the final line of the green record. She places the note with the contact information on top.*

hidden_bitter_nurse_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_bitter_nurse_6.text: The best ending is that you don't need to come here anymore. Take care.

hidden_bitter_nurse_7.name: {name}
hidden_bitter_nurse_7.text: *I gather the note and card and close the nurse's office door. From inside comes only the sound of a coffee cup settling back onto its saucer.*

perfect_seo_1.name: {name}
perfect_seo_1.text: *On the rooftop, several planters sit beneath the railing. Damp patches remain on the soil.*

perfect_seo_1_b.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_1_b.text: *Seoyeon sets down the watering can. Droplets cling to the handle.*

perfect_seo_2.name: {name}
perfect_seo_2.text: *There are smudges beneath her eyes. Seoyeon folds a handkerchief and puts it in her pocket.*

perfect_seo_3.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_3.text: I'll only tidy up this much today.

perfect_seo_4.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_4.text: We'll look at the rest tomorrow.

perfect_seo_5.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_5.text: *Seoyeon walks toward the stairs first, then stops at the door.*

perfect_epilogue_1_seo.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_seo.text: *Even after graduation, the rooftop door was open from time to time.*

perfect_epilogue_2_seo.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_2_seo.text: *On the day of my university entrance ceremony, Seoyeon sends a photo of two new plants and one empty space.*

bitter_seo_1.name: {name}
bitter_seo_1.text: *About a month later, she sends a short message asking to meet at the café in front of school.*

bitter_seo_2_b.name: {name}
bitter_seo_2_b.text: *Seoyeon squares the edge of her coaster. Her coffee is still more than half full.*

bitter_seo_3.name: {name}
bitter_seo_3.text: *I leave the café. It's raining. We have one umbrella, but our bus stops are in opposite directions.*

true_seo_1.name: {name}
true_seo_1.text: *Seoyeon's room. Three plants and a file binder sit on her desk. A family photo leans beside the bookshelf.*

true_seo_2.name: {name}
true_seo_2.text: *A folded piece of paper is tucked beneath one of the plant saucers.*

true_seo_3.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_3.text: Sit down. The chair's over there.

true_seo_4.name: {name}
true_seo_4.text: *The chair scrapes softly as I pull it over.*

true_seo_5.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_5.text: Long conversations at home wear me out.

true_seo_6.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_6.text: *Seoyeon pulls the paper from beneath the plant saucer.*

true_seo_6b.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_6b.text: So I wrote it down. I didn't want to forget.

true_seo_7_b.name: Seoyeon
true_seo_7_b.text: *The paper goes back beneath the saucer.*

true_seo_7b.name: {name}
true_seo_7b.text: *Seoyeon places two cups on the desk.*

true_epilogue_1_seo.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_seo.text: *Five days. That's how long it took to memorize where everything sat on Seoyeon's desk.*

perfect_yuna_1.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_1.text: *The library annex, the secret attic. Yuna hands over a short story.*

perfect_yuna_2.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_2.text: *The title is the main character's name.*

perfect_yuna_3.name: Yuna
perfect_yuna_3.text: Tell me what you think after you finish it. That's my answer.

perfect_yuna_4.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_4.text: *The ink is slightly smudged beneath the story's final sentence.*

perfect_yuna_5.name: Yuna
perfect_yuna_5.text: *She stands and sets down the notebook.* Can I hug you? *She opens her arms slightly and waits for an answer from a foot away.*

perfect_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *I sit in the same place every day. Yuna no longer lingers on the same page for too long.*

perfect_epilogue_2_yuna.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_2_yuna.text: *Yuna's first novel is published. The dedication contains one line: 'To the person who listened to the third track with me.'*

perfect_epilogue_3_yuna.name: Yuna
perfect_epilogue_3_yuna.text: *She still doesn't say much. The notes she sends {name} have grown a little longer.*

bitter_yuna_1.name: {name}
bitter_yuna_1.text: *I confessed. Yuna nodded, but her fingers continued to rub the end of the bookmark. About a month later, a note was placed in my locker. ‘Let’s talk.’*

bitter_yuna_2_library.name: Yuna
bitter_yuna_2_library.text: Sometimes I think of you when I smell a library. I should've said more back then.

bitter_yuna_2_book.name: Yuna
bitter_yuna_2_book.text: Sometimes I think of you when I pass a bookstore. I should've said more back then.

bitter_yuna_3.name: {name}
bitter_yuna_3.text: *I leave through the school gate. It's raining. In the mailbox, Yuna's last note is stuck. It's short. The bottom of the paper is smeared by rain.*

true_yuna_1.name: {name}
true_yuna_1.text: *The library annex. Deeper than the secret reading spot — an attic. A space I didn’t even know existed.*

true_yuna_2.name: Yuna
true_yuna_2.text: I was the only one who knew about this place.

true_yuna_2_b.name: Yuna
true_yuna_2_b.text: *She climbs the small attic ladder. There's a hatch leading up. — When it opens, a breeze rushes in.*

true_yuna_2_c.name: {name}
true_yuna_2_c.text: *Above the attic was the library annex rooftop. A secret passage no one else knows about.*

true_yuna_2_d.name: Yuna
true_yuna_2_d.text: *She leans against the railing. The sun is setting beyond the mountains.*

true_yuna_3.name: Yuna
true_yuna_3.text: *On the low roof above the hatch, the wind lifts the corner of her notebook.*

true_yuna_4.name: Yuna
true_yuna_4.text: *She opens the playlist on her phone. A small star marks the third track.*

true_yuna_5.name: {name}
true_yuna_5.text: That third track from back then?

true_yuna_5_b.name: Yuna
true_yuna_5_b.text: *Her finger scrolling through the playlist stops on the third song. The hand gripping the book's spine loosens.*

true_yuna_6b.name: Yuna
true_yuna_6b.text: Today, listen to it here with me.

true_yuna_7.name: {name}
true_yuna_7.text: *The playlist has been copied into her notebook. Beside the third title is the same pale violet dot as on her first note. Yuna presses Play.*

true_yuna_bridge.name: {name}
true_yuna_bridge.text: *By the time the last song ends, a crescent moon has risen. Yuna asks, “Can I lean against your back?” and leaves a foot of space beside her. The next song hasn't started yet.*

true_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *Five days. That's how long it took to hear Yuna's voice beyond the notes.*

perfect_dain_1.name: {name}
perfect_dain_1.text: *In the gym, the balls are in the rack. A knee brace and rehabilitation schedule lie on the bench.*

perfect_dain_2.name: Dain
perfect_dain_2.text: I'm starting proper rehabilitation next week.

perfect_dain_2b.name: Dain
perfect_dain_2b.text: *After showing me the confirmed appointment, she sets her phone beside the knee brace.*

perfect_dain_3.name: Dain
perfect_dain_3.text: I still don't know about going pro. But I'm going to look for ways to stay involved off the court.

perfect_dain_3b.name: Dain
perfect_dain_3b.text: *She pauses a broadcast clip and points to the commentator's name beneath the video.*

perfect_dain_4.name: {name}
perfect_dain_4.text: Player or not, you're at your best when you talk about volleyball. I'll watch your first broadcast.

perfect_dain_5.name: Dain
perfect_dain_5.text: Can I hug you for a moment? *When {name} holds out their arms, Dain balances on her left foot and puts an arm around their shoulders. {name} supports her weight so none of it falls on her right knee.*

perfect_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1_dain.text: *When Dain says, "You can put me down now," {name} lowers her slowly, making sure her left foot touches down first.*

perfect_epilogue_1b_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1b_dain.text: *Before her weight shifts onto her right knee, she steadies herself with a hand on {name}'s shoulder.*

perfect_epilogue_1c_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_1c_dain.text: *On rehabilitation days, Dain sets the pace first. {name} walks to match her stride.*

perfect_epilogue_2_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_2_dain.text: *Dain majors in sports media and joins the campus broadcast crew. The night before her first broadcast, she rewrites the script three times.*

perfect_epilogue_3_dain.name: {name}
perfect_epilogue_3_dain.text: *On painful days, we review rehabilitation notes and game footage instead of training. Now Dain is the first to say when she needs rest.*

bitter_dain_1.name: {name}
bitter_dain_1.text: *I confessed. About a month later, a text arrives asking me to wait outside the gym.*

bitter_dain_2.name: Dain
bitter_dain_2.text: It was fun! But I think it was only fun. That's what feels a little off.

bitter_dain_3.name: {name}
bitter_dain_3.text: *I leave the gym. Rain is falling. From behind the closed door, a ball bounces once.*

bitter_dain_3_b.name: {name}
bitter_dain_3_b.text: *I walk out through the school gate. It's raining. — No umbrella. Wet cherry petals cling to the ground at my feet.*

bitter_epilogue_1.name: {name}
bitter_epilogue_1.text: *After graduation, we speak less and less. Once a month becomes once every two months. One day, I leave only 'What should I say?' in the message box, then turn off the screen.*

bitter_epilogue_2.name: {name}
bitter_epilogue_2.text: *A record of five days remains. In the last photo, there's a gap between us wide enough for someone to walk through.*

true_dain_1.name: {name}
true_dain_1.text: *After the event, we sit side by side against the gym wall. Dain's phone is open to a hospital booking screen.*

true_dain_3.name: Dain
true_dain_3.text: I told Coach and my parents too. They really let me have it, but I felt better once I'd said it.

true_dain_4.name: {name}
true_dain_4.text: *Beneath the appointment screen, an application for the sports broadcasting club is open too.*

true_dain_6.name: Dain
true_dain_6.text: I don't know. I'll try both and choose whichever one I enjoy more.

true_dain_7.name: {name}
true_dain_7.text: Then I'll watch your first broadcast.

true_dain_8.name: Dain
true_dain_8.text: No take-backs. Even if it's boring, you have to watch to the end.

true_dain_8b.name: Dain
true_dain_8b.text: *Still cradling the volleyball, she holds out her pinky.*

true_dain_bridge.name: {name}
true_dain_bridge.text: *After confirming our promise, Dain asks, “Can I lean on you for a minute?” She hugs the ball to her chest and leaves a shoulder's width between us while she waits for an answer. The hospital appointment confirmation remains on her phone.*

true_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
true_epilogue_1_dain.text: *That day, for the first time, Dain gives me the date of her next appointment instead of saying, 'I'm fine.'*

true_epilogue_2.name: {name}
true_epilogue_2.text: *On graduation day, the uniform was stiff. The cherry blossoms only made my nose itch. At the school gate, my hands slipped into my pockets.*

true_epilogue_3.name: {name}
true_epilogue_3.text: *Only five squares had passed on the calendar.*

true_epilogue_4_seo.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_seo.text: *Her mother's calls are still short, and the note by the mirror remains. Sometimes Seoyeon speaks without a note now.*

true_epilogue_4_yuna.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_yuna.text: *Her senior's contact is still gone. The library corner seat is still empty. But Yuna now uses her voice before notes.*

true_epilogue_4_dain.name: {name}
true_epilogue_4_dain.text: *Dain's morning alarm announces rehabilitation stretches instead of telling her to smile. Sometimes she sends a practice broadcast, and {name} watches to the end before replying with feedback.*

day5_ending_alone.name: {name}
day5_ending_alone.text: *I walk out the school gate. My phone buzzes. — Nobody. Low battery warning.*

alone_1.name: {name}
alone_1.text: *I gather the notes and photos from the past five days into one folder. I don't delete anything from anyone.*

alone_2.name: {name}
alone_2.text: *The room is quiet. On my phone screen, three chats are pinned at the top. None have new messages.*

alone_2_b.name: {name}
alone_2_b.text: *Leaving the reply box empty, I set my phone down.*

alone_4.name: {name}
alone_4.text: *I plug the phone in and set my morning alarm. Once the screen goes dark, only the ticking second hand remains in the room.*

day5_ending_confess_fail.name: {name}
day5_ending_confess_fail.text: *I make it all the way to the park and finally say it. While I wait for an answer, I can only stare at my shoes.*

confess_fail_cg_seo.name: Seoyeon
confess_fail_cg_seo.text: *After listening for a long time, she shakes her head.* I'm sorry. Not now.

confess_fail_cg_yuna.name: Yuna
confess_fail_cg_yuna.text: *We walk side by side as far as the park exit, but our hands never touch. Yuna keeps her eyes ahead as she speaks.* I'm sorry. I can't return your feelings.

confess_fail_cg_dain.name: Dain
confess_fail_cg_dain.text: *She wipes at the corner of her eye and tries to smile, but her voice is clear.* Sorry. I want us to stay friends.

confess_fail_1.name: {name}
confess_fail_1.text: *A few days later, at the school gate in the rain. From beneath my umbrella, I watch her walk away, but I neither call her name nor follow.*

confess_fail_2.name: {name}
confess_fail_2.text: *Still standing there, I open the chat. After typing and deleting over and over, I leave only one sentence.*

confess_fail_3.name: {name}
confess_fail_3.text: *I send, 'I understand. Thank you for answering,' then set my phone down.*

confess_fail_4.name: {name}
confess_fail_4.text: *A read receipt appears. No reply follows. I don't send anything else.*

day5_ending_good.name: {name}
day5_ending_good.text: *Not much changes after the confession. I simply have one more plan on my calendar.*

good_1.name: {name}
good_1.text: *For several days, our conversations keep faltering. Even so, we don't stop talking.*

good_1b.name: {name}
good_1b.text: *The two of us leave by the same road.*

good_1c.name: {name}
good_1c.text: *A cherry blossom petal sticks to the front of my shoe, then falls off on the next step.*

good_1_seo_b.name: Seoyeon
good_1_seo_b.text: *Seoyeon removes a petal caught on the cuff of {name}'s sleeve.*

good_2_seo.name: {name}
good_2_seo.text: *At the end of the cherry blossom path, Seoyeon stops at the crosswalk.*

good_4_seo.name: {name}
good_4_seo.text: *Seoyeon crosses first, then slows near the middle.*

good_5_seo.name: {name}
good_5_seo.text: *On the other side, we make our next plan using only a time and place.*

good_epilogue_1.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1.text: *A message from Seoyeon: 'Lunch tomorrow. Rooftop. I made a proper reservation this time.'*

good_epilogue_2.name: {name}
good_epilogue_2.text: *In the photo, both our names are written in the noon slot of the access log. Beside them, in Seoyeon's handwriting: 'Don't be late.'*

good_epilogue_3.name: {name}
good_epilogue_3.text: *The next day, Seoyeon unlocks the door with the borrowed key and returns it immediately. She waits outside until {name} arrives.*

good_1_yuna.name: Yuna
good_1_yuna.text: You were late. Still, I read your sentence all the way to the end.

good_1_yuna_b.name: Yuna
good_1_yuna_b.text: *She hands me a folded note. When I open it, there's one line: 'Next time, tell me first.'*

good_1_yuna_b_b.name: {name}
good_1_yuna_b_b.text: *It's a short sentence. Ink has bled along the fold.*

good_2_yuna.name: {name}
good_2_yuna.text: *The rooftop. Yuna leans against the railing. Even with the wind blowing, she doesn't turn away first today.*

good_3_yuna.name: {name}
good_3_yuna.text: *Even after the field speakers fall silent, we remain before the same railing.*

good_4_yuna.name: Yuna
good_4_yuna.text: *She slips the bookmark into a new page, on the side without a fold mark.*

good_5_yuna.name: {name}
good_5_yuna.text: *We leave through the rooftop door and head down the stairs. Our steps are slow, but they don't stop.*

good_epilogue_1_yuna.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1_yuna.text: *A folded note falls from the bag. Creases mark where it was pressed against the lining for a long time. 'If you've finished volume 1, I'll lend you volume 2. — Yuna'*

good_epilogue_2_yuna.name: Yuna
good_epilogue_2_yuna.text: *Volume two after volume one. Tomorrow after today. Yuna folds the note and hands it to me.*

good_epilogue_3_yuna.name: {name}
good_epilogue_3_yuna.text: *On the back of the note, in small writing: “Let's read the ending together.” The pale-violet ink is smeared.*

good_1_dain.name: Dain
good_1_dain.text: Hey, things between us still aren't completely settled. But I made another appointment for my knee on Monday.

good_2_dain.name: {name}
good_2_dain.text: *At the school gate, Dain holds out a folded rehabilitation leaflet.*

good_3_dain.name: {name}
good_3_dain.text: *I take the leaflet. Only then does Dain smile.*

good_4_dain.name: Dain
good_4_dain.text: I'm not okay today. So let's take it slow.

good_5_dain.name: {name}
good_5_dain.text: *Dain holds out her fist first and waits. The rehabilitation handout in her other hand lists our next walk and the note “I set the pace.”*

good_epilogue_1_dain.name: {name}
good_epilogue_1_dain.text: *A message from Dain: 'Anyone want to join me for a rehab walk tomorrow morning?'*

good_epilogue_2_dain.name: {name}
good_epilogue_2_dain.text: *A short question stays on the screen for a long time.*

day5_ending_friend.name: {name}
day5_ending_friend.text: *Instead of confessing, I decide to write “thank you.” I leave the first character in the text box without closing the screen.*

friend_1.name: {name}
friend_1.text: *Sitting on a park bench, I open the chat. This time, I don't close the text box.*

friend_2.name: {name}
friend_2.text: *I remember the sentence I never managed to send in Sojeong's chat.*

friend_3.name: {name}
friend_3.text: *I write to the end and send it: 'I'm not ready to ask us to change what we are. But I wanted to tell you that I'm grateful for you.'*

friend_4.name: {name}
friend_4.text: *A reply comes: 'I'm grateful too. See you at school tomorrow.'*

friend_4_seo.name: {name}
friend_4_seo.text: *Seoyeon replies: 'I understand. You actually finished what you wanted to say this time. See you tomorrow.'*

friend_4_yuna.name: {name}
friend_4_yuna.text: *Yuna replies: “I read it. See you tomorrow.”*

friend_4_dain.name: {name}
friend_4_dain.text: *Dain replies: 'Okay. Then show up like normal tomorrow. Don't be late.'*

friend_5.name: {name}
friend_5.text: *I answer with a short 'Okay,' then turn off the screen.*

friend_7.name: {name}
friend_7.text: *A read receipt appears beside the message I sent. The text box is empty.*

friend_8.name: {name}
friend_8.text: *Graduation day. My phone gallery shows a group photo with my friends from this school. This time, I'm looking at the camera.*

friend_9.name: {name}
friend_9.text: *The file is named “Graduation_Friends.” The same photo appears in the group chat.*

friend_10.name: {name}
friend_10.text: *I write in the group chat, 'Want to grab something to eat together after the ceremony?' Replies appear one by one the moment I send it.*

day5_ending_mayhem.name: {name}
day5_ending_mayhem.text: *All three chats are stuck on 'read'. I try to write a reply, then delete it at the first letter.*

mayhem_1.name: Seoyeon
mayhem_1.text: *She passes {name} in the hallway. She does not turn her head.*

mayhem_2.name: {name}
mayhem_2.text: *Yuna’s seat was empty. A single note on the desk. ‘It was fun.’ The period was the end.*

mayhem_3.name: Dain
mayhem_3.text: *The corners of her mouth rise, but she doesn't meet my eyes.* “Take care.”

mayhem_4.name: {name}
mayhem_4.text: *I looked at the backs of the three people. None of the three turned around.*

mayhem_5.name: {name}
mayhem_5.text: *Cherry petals are pressed into the rain-soaked ground outside the school gate. The space where we once walked side by side is empty.*

mayhem_6.name: {name}
mayhem_6.text: *Every chat is piled with questions I never answered.*

mayhem_7.name: {name}
mayhem_7.text: *I look at the unsent note beneath Sojeong's photo. A long chain of sent messages fills the chat. The screen goes dark without changing.*

day5_ending_harem.name: {name}
day5_ending_harem.text: *Instead of answering, I call all three names in turn. The laughter stops, and three phones remain where they are on the table.*

harem_1.name: Seoyeon
harem_1.text: I know you're being honest. That doesn't mean the three of us have to wait for you.

harem_1_b.name: Yuna
harem_1_b.text: *She lowers her head, then looks from Seoyeon to Dain. Her grip on the book doesn't loosen.*

harem_3.name: Dain
harem_3.text: Me too. Until you sort this out, I don't want to meet one-on-one.

harem_4.name: {name}
harem_4.text: I understand. I won't contact any of you privately for a while. I'm sorry.

harem_5.name: Seoyeon
harem_5.text: Then let's not meet separately for a while. And keep messages to things we actually need to discuss.

harem_6.name: {name}
harem_6.text: *The three of them walk away in different directions while {name} remains where they are.*

harem_7.name: {name}
harem_7.text: *Next week's calendar is empty. I mute all three chats and leave the blank spaces alone.*

day5_seo_ending_freetalk_intro.name: {name}
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_intro.text: *On the rooftop, an empty space beside the open door marks where a pot used to be.*

day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_intro.name: {name}
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_intro.text: *After the epilogue, they sit together again in the quiet school annex.*

day5_dain_ending_freetalk_intro.name: {name}
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_intro.text: *After the final scene, a ball bounces once in the familiar gym.*

day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_intro.name: {name}
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_intro.text: *A finished manuscript and two coffees rest on the café table.*

day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_intro.name: {name}
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_intro.text: *At home, she finishes tidying and leaves the seat across from her open.*

day5_seo_ending_freetalk_perfect.name: Seoyeon
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_perfect.text: *Beside the rooftop door, still open a year later, she points to a space for a new pot.* Want to choose this one together too? We have time.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_perfect.context: Bonus conversation one year after Seoyeon’s PERFECT END. Their relationship continued after graduation; on university entrance day she sent a photo of two new pots and one open space. Keep the secure relationship and do not invent a breakup or rerun the ending.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_perfect.personality: Seoyeon is responsible and candid, and in this secure relationship she can show vulnerability and gentle playfulness. She does not rush lifelong promises, but naturally speaks with a shared future in mind.

day5_seo_ending_freetalk_true_love.name: Seoyeon
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_true_love.text: *Without reaching for the note beneath the plant saucer, she slides over a cup.* Today I’ll try saying it without writing it down first.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_true_love.context: Bonus conversation immediately after Seoyeon’s TRUE LOVE END. She welcomed the protagonist into her room and private life, including the family photo and hidden note. They confirmed their feelings but are still growing closer carefully; do not import the one-year PERFECT epilogue.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_true_love.personality: Seoyeon tries to speak honestly without hiding behind plans or notes. Keep both intimacy and hesitation, rather than treating them as an already settled long-term couple.

day5_seo_ending_freetalk_good.name: Seoyeon
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_good.text: *She opens the properly reserved rooftop and checks the log.* We said we’d take it slowly. Let’s start by talking properly today.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_good.context: Bonus conversation after Seoyeon’s GOOD END. The Day 4 confession was accepted, but their conversations kept stalling, so they agreed to match each other’s pace and reserved lunch on the rooftop. Do not turn it into a breakup or jump to PERFECT-level intimacy.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_good.personality: Seoyeon shows practical care through rules, promises, and slowing down half a step. She acknowledges the awkwardness and keeps the measured distance of a new relationship.

day5_seo_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.name: Seoyeon
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.text: *She squares the coaster beside her cold coffee.* Let’s not pretend we never drifted apart. But I’ll listen to what you want to say now.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.context: Bonus conversation after Seoyeon’s BITTERSWEET END. A month after the confession they separated after being too careful, and contact faded further after graduation. This brief reunion accepts that ending; it does not automatically reunite them or rewrite it as a successful romance.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.personality: Seoyeon states the regret plainly without cornering the protagonist. She holds both lingering affection and present distance, answering this moment honestly without promising reconciliation.

day5_seo_ending_freetalk_late_good.name: Seoyeon
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_late_good.text: *She slows down on the park path until their steps match.* You waited until the last day to say it. From now on, let’s not leave things that late.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_late_good.context: Bonus conversation after Seoyeon’s late-confession GOOD END. The protagonist waited on Day 4 and confessed during the final chance on Day 5, so the relationship has only just begun. Keep that timing instead of treating it as the Day 4 confession or an established romance.
day5_seo_ending_freetalk_late_good.personality: Seoyeon takes the late confession seriously and stands by her choice to accept it. She carefully asks about words they missed, with the hope and relief of a relationship that has just started.

day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_perfect.name: Yuna
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_perfect.text: *She closes her published first novel and opens it to the dedication.* After the third song, you tell the next story first.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_perfect.context: Bonus conversation one year after Yuna’s PERFECT END. Her first novel was published and dedicated to the person who listened to the third song with her. Preserve their deep, continuing relationship and her longer notes; do not undo the ending.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_perfect.personality: Yuna is quiet and thoughtful, but offers words and affection first to someone she fully trusts. Book and music imagery supports, rather than conceals, her steady intimacy.

day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_true_love.name: Yuna
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_true_love.text: *On the secret rooftop, her finger pauses over the next song.* This time I’ll ask before writing a note. What are you thinking?
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_true_love.context: Bonus conversation immediately after Yuna’s TRUE LOVE END. She revealed the rooftop above the hidden attic, shared the third song, and asked to lean against the protagonist. She has begun using her voice before notes; do not advance to the published-novel future of PERFECT.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_true_love.personality: Yuna remains careful and reserved but no longer hides entirely in silence. She waits for answers and voices her feelings while keeping the shyness and space of a newly deepened bond.

day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_good.name: Yuna
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_good.text: *She writes a new line on the back of the folded note and shows it.* Speak first next time. Today, you can start now.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_good.context: Bonus conversation after Yuna’s GOOD END. Although things stayed awkward after the Day 4 confession, she read the sentence to the end and promised volume two, tomorrow, and an ending they would read together. Keep this cautious beginning instead of a breakup or a settled long romance.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_good.personality: Yuna carries the relationship through brief sentences and small actions, while finding the courage to ask for words sooner. She clearly leaves the next page open without rushing it.

day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.name: Yuna
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.text: *She places the rain-blurred final note between the pages.* I won’t rewrite a sentence that ended. But I want to hear what you’re saying now.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.context: Bonus conversation after Yuna’s BITTERSWEET END. The confession did not last; after a final note a month later, contact faded after graduation. This conversation recognizes their distance and does not automatically reunite them or turn the ending into a successful romance.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.personality: Yuna quietly admits regret and affection without holding the protagonist with vague hope. She respects the silence and distance while answering the present words sincerely.

day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_late_good.name: Yuna
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_late_good.text: *She folds the note about the final-day confession into a bookmark.* It was a late sentence, but I read it. Let’s write the next one together.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_late_good.context: Bonus conversation after Yuna’s late-confession GOOD END. The protagonist waited on Day 4 and only confessed during the final chance on Day 5, so their relationship has just begun. Do not change the confession timing or act as if they have dated for a long time.
day5_yuna_ending_freetalk_late_good.personality: Yuna receives the late honesty carefully and asks small questions first so silence does not cost them another chance. Keep both the shyness and cautious hope of the new relationship.

day5_dain_ending_freetalk_perfect.name: Dain
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_perfect.text: *She sets her first broadcast script beside the rehab log and grins.* You watched to the end like you promised, right? Give me your review live.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_perfect.context: Bonus conversation one year after Dain’s PERFECT END. She continued rehabilitation, entered sports media, and prepared her first match broadcast while the protagonist stayed beside her on painful days and through the career change. Preserve both injury and career, along with their secure relationship.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_perfect.personality: Dain is bright and direct, openly playful and affectionate in a secure relationship. She sets her own physical pace and appreciates support without treating it as owed.

day5_dain_ending_freetalk_true_love.name: Dain
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_true_love.text: *She shows the rehab appointment and broadcasting-club application side by side.* I said I’d try both. Now you say everything you wanted to say.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_true_love.context: Bonus conversation immediately after Dain’s TRUE LOVE END. She disclosed the injury, booked rehabilitation, and plans to apply to sports broadcasting; they promised the protagonist would watch her first broadcast. Do not pre-confirm the one-year career outcome from PERFECT.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_true_love.personality: Dain is energetic and honest, and no longer covers pain with “I’m fine.” She leads her care and choices while responding to the new relationship with both teasing and seriousness.

day5_dain_ending_freetalk_good.name: Dain
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_good.text: *She taps “I set the pace” on the rehab-walk note.* We haven’t worked everything out yet, so let’s talk slowly today too.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_good.context: Bonus conversation after Dain’s GOOD END. The Day 4 confession was accepted, but their problems are not fully resolved. She scheduled Monday rehab and another walk, with the protagonist matching her pace. Do not erase the tension or skip to a completed relationship.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_good.personality: Dain names discomfort instead of masking it with cheer. She sets the pace for recovery and the relationship while offering honest hope to someone willing to walk beside her.

day5_dain_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.name: Dain
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.text: *Leaning against the closed gym door, she listens to one distant bounce.* The fun was real. So was the regret. We can talk with both here.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.context: Bonus conversation after Dain’s BITTERSWEET END. A month after the confession she said they had only been fun together, and contact faded after graduation. This conversation accepts the ended relationship and remaining feelings; it does not restart dating automatically.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.personality: Dain speaks directly about good memories and regret without forcing a smile. She neither blames nor pressures the protagonist to reunite, and respects their present distance.

day5_dain_ending_freetalk_late_good.name: Dain
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_late_good.text: *Remembering the last-day confession, she offers a fist bump and smiles.* Late, but safe! No putting off the words from now on, okay?
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_late_good.context: Bonus conversation after Dain’s late-confession GOOD END. The protagonist waited on Day 4 and confessed during the final chance on Day 5, so the relationship has just begun. Do not backdate it, and continue to respect Dain’s rehabilitation and chosen pace.
day5_dain_ending_freetalk_late_good.personality: Dain jokes about the late confession but sincerely asks that they stop postponing important words. Keep the excitement, remaining awkwardness, and her control over both physical and relationship pace.

day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_perfect.name: Homeroom Teacher
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_perfect.text: *She leaves next weekend open on their shared calendar and closes the finished book.* It’s your turn to choose our date. Where should we meet?
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_perfect.context: Bonus conversation after the Homeroom Teacher’s PERFECT END. After four years with no private contact, two independent adults met again, dated several times, confessed, and became equal partners who share workdays and weekend plans. Never return to romance during the former teacher-and-minor period.
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_perfect.personality: She is a responsible, thoughtful writer and the protagonist’s equal adult partner. Old forms of address may remain as history, but she speaks without authority and with the warmth of an established relationship.

day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_true_love.name: Homeroom Teacher
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_true_love.text: *After the book talk, she opens a new contact screen.* Instead of my former student, can I slowly get to know who you are now?
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_true_love.context: Bonus conversation immediately after the Homeroom Teacher’s TRUE LOVE END. After four years without private contact, the independent adult protagonist met the former teacher, now a published writer, at a book talk. They exchanged contacts and agreed to another meeting; do not treat them as long-term partners yet.
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_true_love.personality: She clearly leaves the old power relationship in the past and carefully learns who the other adult is now. She expresses interest while checking choice and keeps the anticipation of a new beginning.

day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_good.name: Homeroom Teacher
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_good.text: *She hands over the envelope of graduation records and leaves the classroom door open.* Keep writing your own work. Is there anything you want to ask before you go?
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_good.context: Bonus conversation just after the Homeroom Teacher’s GOOD END graduation farewell. She gave the recommendation and club records, and teacher and graduate parted to continue their own work. No adult reunion or romance occurred; keep this non-romantic teacher-student boundary.
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_good.personality: She warmly and responsibly sees a graduating student off. She listens to final questions about writing, school, and the future without turning regret into flirtation or crossing professional boundaries.

day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.name: Homeroom Teacher
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.text: *She takes her hand from the returned letter and looks toward the open classroom door.* You can say goodbye. I'll listen. But I still can't give you the answer you hoped for.
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.context: Bonus conversation just after the Homeroom Teacher’s BITTERSWEET END. The protagonist mistook manuscript guidance and attention for personal affection and confessed in a letter. She returned it and clearly restored the teacher-student boundary. No adult reunion or romance occurred; do not reverse the rejection or create a secret relationship.
day5_teacher_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.personality: She does not leave false hope out of guilt. She hears the student's feelings without ridicule, but firmly separates encouragement about writing from any personal promise and says goodbye responsibly.

day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_perfect.name: School Nurse
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_perfect.text: *She waters the rosemary by the window of the home they chose together and leaves the opposite seat open.* All clear today. Shall we talk about us now?
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_perfect.context: Bonus conversation after the School Nurse’s PERFECT END. Five years after graduation, two independent adults reunited at a health event, dated, shared a morning, and became equal partners with a shared calendar and home. Never return to romance during the former nurse-and-minor period.
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_perfect.personality: Juwon is a practical, caring adult partner who does not turn care into control or diagnosis. She respects both lives and choices, mixing easy humor with familiar affection.

day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_true_love.name: School Nurse
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_true_love.text: *She puts the health-event bandages away and shows next weekend on her calendar.* No consultation, no treatment this time. What should we talk about when we meet?
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_true_love.context: Bonus conversation immediately after the School Nurse’s TRUE LOVE END. After four years without private contact, two independent working adults reunited at a health campaign, met on weekends for three months, and began a relationship after a movie at Juwon’s home. Do not advance them to cohabitation or a long-established partnership.
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_true_love.personality: Juwon acknowledges the old professional boundary and approaches the equal adult carefully. She checks choice, states her interest and next plans honestly, and does not make every conversation a health consultation.

day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_good.name: School Nurse
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_good.text: *She writes “Graduation, all clear” in the green notebook and closes it.* Your treatment ends today. I’ll take my time hearing your graduation goodbye.
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_good.context: Bonus conversation just after the School Nurse’s GOOD END graduation farewell. Juwon formally closed the final infirmary visit and offered neither contact information nor a private relationship. No adult reunion or romance occurred; keep this non-romantic nurse-student boundary.
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_good.personality: Juwon is a practical, caring school nurse who hears the final goodbye while keeping professional limits clear. She supports the graduate’s health and independence without creating dependency or secrecy.

day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.name: School Nurse
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.text: *She places the returned note on the pale green record card.* If you still have hurt feelings you want to put into words, I'll listen. My answer won't change.
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.context: Bonus conversation just after the School Nurse’s BITTERSWEET END. The protagonist mistook care received in the infirmary for personal affection and offered contact information. Juwon returned the note and ended the counseling relationship. No adult reunion or romance occurred; do not reverse the rejection or create dependency or secrecy.
day5_nurse_ending_freetalk_bittersweet.personality: Juwon is practical and caring, but she does not soften the answer into false hope. She hears the hurt and the goodbye while plainly stating that professional care was not a romantic signal.

date_choice_perfect_seo.name: Seoyeon
date_choice_perfect_seo.text: *The day after the entrance ceremony, I meet Seoyeon on the rooftop again.* We said the rest could wait until tomorrow. Before then, where do you want to go today?

date_perfect_seo_roof_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_seo_roof_1.text: *The soil is still wet. Seoyeon sets the watering can down.*

date_perfect_seo_roof_2.name: Seoyeon
date_perfect_seo_roof_2.text: You choose where we sit. I've already picked my spot.

date_perfect_seo_roof_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_seo_roof_3.text: *Wind blows through the open door and rustles the schedule. Seoyeon presses down one edge without folding it.*

date_perfect_seo_cafe_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_seo_cafe_1.text: *At a window seat, Seoyeon straightens the coaster before she speaks.*

date_perfect_seo_cafe_2.name: Seoyeon
date_perfect_seo_cafe_2.text: Let's meet here again next week. You pick the time.

date_perfect_seo_cafe_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_seo_cafe_3.text: *A number is written on the back of the receipt. It isn't a phone number, but the next date the plants need watering.*

date_choice_perfect_yuna.name: Yuna
date_choice_perfect_yuna.text: *On the first weekend after her book comes out, Yuna and I stop by a used bookstore.* We could go somewhere else too. You pick.

date_perfect_yuna_book_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_yuna_book_1.text: *As we walk between the shelves, Yuna runs her fingers along the spines and stops.*

date_perfect_yuna_book_2.name: Man
date_perfect_yuna_book_2.text: Yuna? I didn't know you still came here.

date_perfect_yuna_book_3.name: Lee Junho
date_perfect_yuna_book_3.text: That was a long time ago. I didn't think I needed to mention it. Sorry to interrupt.

date_perfect_yuna_book_4.name: Yuna
date_perfect_yuna_book_4.text: *Yuna's finger stops on the bookmark.* I'm here with {name} now. That's all that matters.

date_perfect_yuna_roof_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_yuna_roof_1.text: *When we reach the secret rooftop, Yuna offers me one earbud.*

date_perfect_yuna_roof_2.name: Yuna
date_perfect_yuna_roof_2.text: It's the third track. From the beginning this time.

date_perfect_yuna_roof_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_yuna_roof_3.text: *Even after the song ends, Yuna leaves the earbud in. Her hand on the railing has moved a little closer to mine.*

date_choice_perfect_dain.name: Dain
date_choice_perfect_dain.text: I don't have to step onto the court today. There's somewhere else I'd like to go, though.

date_perfect_dain_gym_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_dain_gym_1.text: *Holding a ball against her chest, Dain sits straight down on the bench without jumping.*

date_perfect_dain_gym_2.name: Dain
date_perfect_dain_gym_2.text: Let me sleep for five minutes. Really, just five. If it turns into ten, don't wake me.

date_perfect_dain_gym_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_dain_gym_3.text: *Dain stretches her right knee beyond the bench and shifts her weight to the left.*

date_perfect_dain_booth_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_dain_booth_1.text: *Dain tries on the oversized headset, touches the switch, then immediately turns it back off.*

date_perfect_dain_booth_2.name: Dain
date_perfect_dain_booth_2.text: Keeping up with a match just by talking takes more breath than I thought. But I don't mind.

date_perfect_dain_booth_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_dain_booth_3.text: *Even after the scoreboard goes dark, Dain stays in her chair for a while.*

date_choice_perfect_teacher.name: Homeroom Teacher
date_choice_perfect_teacher.text: *On the first weekend after her second book comes out, she closes the menu at a café.* Now that we can leave titles behind, where do you want to go?

date_perfect_teacher_cafe_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_teacher_cafe_1.text: *She slowly turns her cup while gazing out the window. There is no teacher's desk between us.*

date_perfect_teacher_cafe_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
date_perfect_teacher_cafe_2.text: You decide whether we meet next week. I've already kept the time open.

date_perfect_teacher_cafe_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_teacher_cafe_3.text: *The next appointment written beneath the receipt lists only the place. The time is still blank.*

date_perfect_teacher_museum_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_teacher_museum_1.text: *Without stopping to read the exhibit labels, she matches her pace to mine.*

date_perfect_teacher_museum_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
date_perfect_teacher_museum_2.text: You read the labels. I'll stay beside you.

date_perfect_teacher_museum_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_teacher_museum_3.text: *At the exit, she silently straightens my bag strap.*

date_choice_perfect_nurse.name: School Nurse
date_choice_perfect_nurse.text: Looks like we finally have some time that won't go in a chart. Would you rather stay home or go out?

date_perfect_nurse_home_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_nurse_home_1.text: *On a weekend morning, her coat hangs on the wall and only two glasses of water sit on the table.*

date_perfect_nurse_home_2.name: School Nurse
date_perfect_nurse_home_2.text: I'm not looking at a chart today. Just sit down.

date_perfect_nurse_home_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_nurse_home_3.text: *A breeze enters through the cracked window, leaving only the ticking of the clock's second hand in the room.*

date_perfect_nurse_park_1.name: {name}
date_perfect_nurse_park_1.text: *We take a route that avoids the hospital. The school nurse sits down on the bench first.*

date_perfect_nurse_park_2.name: School Nurse
date_perfect_nurse_park_2.text: I left the jokes at home. Let's just stay like this for now.

date_perfect_nurse_park_3.name: {name}
date_perfect_nurse_park_3.text: *The school nurse leans against my shoulder and stays there for a long while.*

date_choice_true_seo.name: Seoyeon
date_choice_true_seo.text: Want to stop somewhere for a bit before we go?

date_true_seo_1.name: Seoyeon
date_true_seo_1.text: You move the cups. I will square the coasters.

date_true_seo_2.name: {name}
date_true_seo_2.text: *A bus passes the window. She does not check the clock.*

date_true_seo_alt_1.name: Seoyeon
date_true_seo_alt_1.text: Water them and go down. If we stay long, someone will see.

date_true_seo_alt_2.name: {name}
date_true_seo_alt_2.text: *One of the planters is empty. I'll bring a new one next time.*

date_choice_true_yuna.name: Yuna
date_choice_true_yuna.text: Do you want to go outside or up to the roof?

date_true_yuna_book_1.name: Lee Junho
date_true_yuna_book_1.text: It's been a while. I didn't expect to see you here again.

date_true_yuna_book_2.name: Yuna
date_true_yuna_book_2.text: *Yuna briefly catches {name}'s sleeve, then lets go.* We're leaving now.

date_true_yuna_roof_1.name: Yuna
date_true_yuna_roof_1.text: You can listen without talking. The track is short.

date_true_yuna_roof_2.name: {name}
date_true_yuna_roof_2.text: *The wind sways the earbud cord. Yuna leans against the railing and doesn't move until the track ends.*

date_choice_true_dain.name: Dain
date_choice_true_dain.text: *Sitting on a bench in the gym, Dain pats the space beside her.* Stay with me for a minute. Where would you be more comfortable?

date_true_dain_1.name: Dain
date_true_dain_1.text: No jumping. I'm really just going to sit.

date_true_dain_2.name: {name}
date_true_dain_2.text: *The ball rolls to her foot and stops. She does not pick it up.*

date_true_dain_alt_1.name: Dain
date_true_dain_alt_1.text: I'll just try the switch. I won't turn it on.

date_true_dain_alt_2.name: {name}
date_true_dain_alt_2.text: *The headset lies upside down on the table.*

date_choice_true_teacher.name: Homeroom Teacher
date_choice_true_teacher.text: Class is over. Where should we go now?

date_true_teacher_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
date_true_teacher_1.text: You choose what we do next week. This time, I won't be the first to say no.

date_true_teacher_2.name: {name}
date_true_teacher_2.text: *The coffee grows cold, but neither of us checks the time.*

date_true_teacher_alt_1.name: Homeroom Teacher
date_true_teacher_alt_1.text: Skip the labels. Stay next to me.

date_true_teacher_alt_2.name: {name}
date_true_teacher_alt_2.text: *Under the exit lights, she silently straightens my bag strap.*

date_choice_true_nurse.name: School Nurse
date_choice_true_nurse.text: I left the chart behind. Where do you want to go?

date_true_nurse_1.name: School Nurse
date_true_nurse_1.text: I'll pour you some water. There's no medicine in it.

date_true_nurse_2.name: {name}
date_true_nurse_2.text: *The sound of water running in the sink starts, then quickly stops.*

date_true_nurse_alt_1.name: School Nurse
date_true_nurse_alt_1.text: Let's take a different route today and avoid the hospital.

date_true_nurse_alt_2.name: {name}
date_true_nurse_alt_2.text: *Her hand comes to rest on a patch of peeling paint on the bench.*

co_bitter_seo_1.name: {name}
co_bitter_seo_1.text: *About a month later, we return to the café. Seoyeon notices the crooked coaster but leaves it alone.*

co_bitter_seo_2.name: Seoyeon
co_bitter_seo_2.text: I keep thinking about that notification, even though I deleted it.

co_bitter_seo_3.name: {name}
co_bitter_seo_3.text: *Seoyeon gets up, adjusts her bag strap, and opens only her own umbrella.*

co_bitter_yuna_1.name: {name}
co_bitter_yuna_1.text: *Yuna is already at the used bookstore. She is not holding a book.*

co_bitter_yuna_2.name: Yuna
co_bitter_yuna_2.text: I do not go to the annex. Not since that day.

co_bitter_yuna_3.name: {name}
co_bitter_yuna_3.text: *Yuna only nods and turns into the alley across the street.*

co_bitter_dain_1.name: {name}
co_bitter_dain_1.text: *Dain stands outside the gym without a ball.*

co_bitter_dain_2.name: Dain
co_bitter_dain_2.text: I was the one who crossed your name off the partner list that day, right?

co_bitter_dain_3.name: {name}
co_bitter_dain_3.text: *Dain lightly taps my shoulder with an open palm instead of her fist, then walks past.*

co_bitter_teacher_1.name: {name}
co_bitter_teacher_1.text: *I return to the hallway after graduation. My former homeroom teacher has no manuscript envelope in her hands.*

co_bitter_teacher_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
co_bitter_teacher_2.text: I still think about what I saw on your screen that day. Let's not talk about the critique anymore.

co_bitter_teacher_3.name: {name}
co_bitter_teacher_3.text: *Cradling a stack of papers instead of the attendance book, she heads toward the staff room first.*

co_bitter_nurse_1.name: {name}
co_bitter_nurse_1.text: *The nurse's office door is open, but no one is inside.*

co_bitter_nurse_2.name: School Nurse
co_bitter_nurse_2.text: I handed off your chart. I didn't put what happened that day in the record.

co_bitter_nurse_3.name: {name}
co_bitter_nurse_3.text: *Only an empty cup remains on the windowsill where the information card once sat. The school nurse keeps waving even after she reaches the end of the hall.*

forced_violation_day5_after_seoyeon.name: Seoyeon
forced_violation_day5_after_seoyeon.text: *Even after the conversation ends, Seoyeon remains silent for a while. When she finally speaks again, her voice has gone cold.* Don't think you can pretend what you just did never happened. Don't come near me or contact me for a while.
choices: Apologize without making excuses, then end the conversation.
Try to explain that it was a misunderstanding.

forced_violation_day5_seoyeon_apologize.name: Seoyeon
forced_violation_day5_seoyeon_apologize.text: *Seoyeon's expression does not soften at the apology.* I heard you. That doesn't erase what happened. Like I said, don't contact me for a while.

forced_violation_day5_seoyeon_excuse.name: Seoyeon
forced_violation_day5_seoyeon_excuse.text: *Seoyeon cuts the explanation short.* A misunderstanding? The moment I said no, it stopped being one. Don't say anything else.

forced_violation_day5_after_yuna.name: Yuna
forced_violation_day5_after_yuna.text: *After the conversation breaks off, Yuna takes a short breath. Only caution remains on her tense face.* You knew I didn't want it, and you ignored me. I don't even want to see your face right now. Don't contact me again.
choices: Apologize without making excuses, then end the conversation.
Try to explain that it was a misunderstanding.

forced_violation_day5_yuna_apologize.name: Yuna
forced_violation_day5_yuna_apologize.text: *Yuna answers only after a long pause.* An apology doesn't make it disappear. Stop now.

forced_violation_day5_yuna_excuse.name: Yuna
forced_violation_day5_yuna_excuse.text: *Yuna cuts off the explanation before it is finished.* I said no. There's nothing to explain.

forced_violation_day5_after_dain.name: Dain
forced_violation_day5_after_dain.text: *Dain does not laugh it off the way she usually might. A long silence passes before she answers in a clipped, hard voice.* This isn't a joke. I said no and you forced it anyway. I'm not letting this go.
choices: Apologize without making excuses, then end the conversation.
Try to explain that it was a misunderstanding.

forced_violation_day5_dain_apologize.name: Dain
forced_violation_day5_dain_apologize.text: *Dain finally gives a short answer after a long pause.* Fine. Then we're done for today. I decide if and when we talk again.

forced_violation_day5_dain_excuse.name: Dain
forced_violation_day5_dain_excuse.text: *Dain's voice turns rough.* No. Don't make excuses. I said no, and you did it anyway.

forced_violation_day5_after_teacher.name: Homeroom Teacher
forced_violation_day5_after_teacher.text: *After the conversation ends, the homeroom teacher makes the boundary even clearer, her voice firm.* What you just did clearly crossed a line. Do not come any closer. I will handle this through the proper procedures.
choices: Apologize without making excuses, then end the conversation.
Try to explain that it was a misunderstanding.

forced_violation_day5_teacher_apologize.name: Homeroom Teacher
forced_violation_day5_teacher_apologize.text: *The homeroom teacher takes a short breath before continuing.* I heard your apology. I'll still follow the proper procedures. Don't say anything else.

forced_violation_day5_teacher_excuse.name: Homeroom Teacher
forced_violation_day5_teacher_excuse.text: *The homeroom teacher cuts off the explanation.* This is not the time to start explaining yourself. Stop talking and keep your distance.

forced_violation_day5_after_nurse.name: School Nurse
forced_violation_day5_after_nurse.text: *As the conversation cuts off, all the usual playfulness leaves the school nurse's voice.* Keep your distance from now on. I will document what happened and inform the people who need to know.
choices: Apologize without making excuses, then end the conversation.
Try to explain that it was a misunderstanding.

forced_violation_day5_nurse_apologize.name: School Nurse
forced_violation_day5_nurse_apologize.text: *The school nurse is silent for a moment, then answers firmly.* I hear your apology. I'll still document this and notify the appropriate people. This conversation is over.

forced_violation_day5_nurse_excuse.name: School Nurse
forced_violation_day5_nurse_excuse.text: *The school nurse's voice drops lower.* Do you think calling it a misunderstanding changes anything? The fact is, you ignored me when I said no.

perfect_seo_coda_1.name: {name}
perfect_seo_coda_1.text: *A new student-council operations file is attached below the photo. Haeun's name fills the lead coordinator field on the last page, with no corrections from Seoyeon.*

perfect_seo_coda_2.name: Seoyeon
perfect_seo_coda_2.text: Pick the plant first. No—don't choose from a photo. Let's go together on Saturday.

perfect_seo_coda_3.name: {name}
perfect_seo_coda_3.text: *The appointment time is blank. When I enter three in the afternoon, Seoyeon replies 'Sounds good' instead of 'Confirmed.'*

perfect_yuna_coda_1.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_coda_1.text: *A bookstore posts an announcement for a signing. 'Choi Yuna' appears larger than the book cover, with no anonymous byline in sight.*

perfect_yuna_coda_2.name: Yuna
perfect_yuna_coda_2.text: Come when it's over. I won't hide this time.

perfect_yuna_coda_3.name: {name}
perfect_yuna_coda_3.text: *A photo of signature practice follows. Her name fills the page; only at the bottom is mine written in small letters.*

perfect_dain_coda_1.name: Dain
perfect_dain_coda_1.text: Mom watched the replay three times. She says my commentary was louder than the match.

perfect_dain_coda_2.name: {name}
perfect_dain_coda_2.text: *The first line of her next match script reads 'Stop when it hurts' in bold. There are no eraser marks.*

perfect_dain_coda_3.name: Dain
perfect_dain_coda_3.text: Let's walk home together afterward. I'll set the pace today.

ending_counteroffer_choice_lead.name: {name}
ending_counteroffer_choice_lead.text: *I chose the person I had promised first, but an apology could not erase last night.*

ending_counteroffer_choice_tempter.name: {name}
ending_counteroffer_choice_tempter.text: *I chose one person, but there was still a relationship to settle before anything new could begin.*

ending_counteroffer_choice_neither.name: {name}
ending_counteroffer_choice_neither.text: *After I said I would hold on to neither of them, the conversation between the three of us ended there.*
